item.title: Why Minds Need Bodies: Organismic Unity and Limits of Artificial Consciousness
item.description: This paper argues that functional organization alone is not sufficient for phenomenal consciousness or the existence of a unified subject of experience. While many contemporary accounts of artificial consciousness assume that replicating the causal or computational structure of the brain would be sufficient for subjective experience, this paper identifies a deeper constraint: consciousness depends on organismic unity.

item.title: Reviewer #2 (Public review): Pupil size reveals the perceptual quality and effortless nature of synesthesia
item.description: Perception feels like a window onto the world, but it never is. What we see is built from what reaches the eye and from what the brain adds. In synesthesia, that second part is easy to spot.

item.title: Gradient usability in few-qubit quantum Neural Networks: A signal-to-noise ratio framework for evaluating mitigation strategies
item.description: The barren-plateau problem—the exponential flattening of optimization landscapes—severely limits the trainability of quantum neural networks (QNNs) on near-term hardware. This review examines ansatz-design and complementary mitigation strategies for few-qubit QNNs under finite-shot noisy intermediate-scale quantum (NISQ) constraints.

item.title: Reviewer #2 (Public review): Neural correlates of perceptual consciousness from within: A narrative review of human intracranial research
item.description: Combining intracranial recordings with no-report paradigms and computational models offers the clearest path yet to isolating genuine neural correlates of consciousness from their prerequisites and consequences.

item.title: Neural correlates of perceptual consciousness from within: A narrative review of human intracranial research
item.description: Despite many years of research, the quest to identify neural correlates of perceptual consciousness (NCC) remains unresolved. One major obstacle lies in methodological limitations: most studies rely on non-invasive neural measures with limited spatial or temporal resolution, making it difficult to disentangle proper NCCs from concurrent cognitive processes.

item.title: EEG-CBF integration in calf slaughter neurophysiology: a narrative review
item.description: Loss of consciousness (LOC) during calf slaughter is a neurophysiological process that requires distinction between cortical awareness and reflexive subcortical or spinal activity. Conscious perception depends on intact thalamocortical connectivity and integrated cortical function.

item.title: Neural Flux Attachment: From Bose Condensates to Chiral Topological Matter
item.description: Can one neural wave function describe both a Bose condensate and a chiral topological liquid? We introduce ChernFormer, which combines a fermionic transformer with a fixed Chern-Simons phase that attaches one statistical vortex to every particle pair.

item.title: How Much Reconstruction Does Quantum Machine Learning Need? Late Fusion of Independently Trained Quantum Subcircuits
item.description: Circuit cutting lets a large quantum neural network (QNN) run as independent subcircuits on small devices, but rebuilding its outputs by reconstruction carries a classical sampling overhead exponential in the number of cuts - the dominant runtime cost in prior work. We ask whether, for machine-learning tasks, this step is necessary, and replace it with late fusion: each subcircuit is trained and measured independently, and a small classical head combines their outputs - a linear-cost, decision-level combination…
